[11/08/2026 1:47 PM] - SESSION CLARIFICATION — HEALTH, COMMITS, BRANCHES, GITHUB, AGENTS.MD

This entry addresses Pete's confusion about what is committed vs uncommitted,
how branches (main / evidence-registry) relate to the system, what GitHub
repos and pull requests mean, how agent memory works, what AGENTS.md is, and
why the system is in its current state.

SECTION 1: COMMITTED vs UNCOMMITTED — WHAT IS HAPPENING RIGHT NOW
------------------------------------------------------------------

* CURRENT STATE (11/08/2026 1:47 PM AEST):
  - Git reports: 96 files changed (1200 lines added, 14844 lines deleted)
  - These changes are UNCOMMITTED. They exist only on your local disk.
  - The last COMMIT was 50029cb ("vista-sec-water: API key vault bridge"),
    made 2026-08-10 23:04 AEST. That is the last permanent snapshot.

* WHAT "COMMITTED" MEANS (plain English):
  - A commit = a permanent saved checkpoint in git's history. Once committed,
    git remembers that exact state forever.
  - "NOT committed" = the file exists on your disk but git has no record of
    it. If you delete the file or your drive fails, it's gone.
  - "STAGED" = files marked as "ready to commit next time." A pre-commit
    checklist. No files are currently staged in this system.

* WHAT IS CHANGED BUT NOT SAVED (the 96 files):
  These fall into THREE categories:

  CATEGORY A — DIRECTORY RENAME (old path → new 4-value path):
  The directory `vista-local-subsystem-root` was renamed to `vista-localsub-root`
  (part of the 4-value ID reform). Git sees the old path files as DELETED and
  the new path files as UNTRACKED (new). The files still exist — they just moved.
  Git does NOT track directory renames automatically. This accounts for ~80 of
  the 96 "changed" files. The files are SAFE — they exist under the new path.
  
  Old: .vscode/pete/vista-local-subsystem-root/*     (deleted in git's view)
  New: .vscode/pete/vista-localsub-root/*             (untracked in git's view)

  CATEGORY B — FILES MODIFIED IN PLACE:
  These files were edited directly and exist at the same location:
    - README.md (rewritten with system architecture + terminology bridge)
    - cloudflare/src/worker.js (vault shim added)
    - crons/openclaw/logs/monitor1.json (auto-updated by scheduler)
    - crons/openclaw/projects.json (auto-updated by scheduler)
    - crons/openclaw/registry/assets.json (auto-updated by scheduler)
    - docker-compose.yml (DOCKER_RUNNING flag added)
    - docs/handbook/handbook-01-setup-installation.md (handbook edits)
    - images/Dockerfile (container config updated)
    - mya/index.html (Mya page revisions)
    - scripts/adc-login.py (ADC login script updated)
    - server.js (vault-bridge wiring added)

  CATEGORY C — BRAND NEW FILES (never tracked by git):
    - AGENTS.md (agent briefing + terminology bridge)
    - vistamations-system.code-workspace (VS Code workspace)
    - .vscode/pete/vista-cloudsub-root/* (Cloudflare + GCloud env roots)
    - .vscode/pete/vista-localsub-root/* (4-value ID restructure)
    - .vscode/pete/vista-localsub-root/vista-localenv-env-root/vista-pete-clarify/pete-clarify.txt (this file)
    - .vscode/pete/vista-localsub-root/vista-localenv-env-root/vista-session-chat/chat-results-4.txt

    - mya/src/* (Mya Cloudflare Worker source)
    - mya/wrangler.toml (Mya Worker config)
    - olivia/* (Olivia dispatch module)
    - cloudflare/src/vault-shim.js (worker secret mapper)
    - and others...

* A note about "commits ahead":
  - Git reports nothing "ahead" right now because evidence-registry has already
    been pushed to GitHub (remote origin/evidence-registry is at the same commit).
  - The "ahead" counter appears when your local branch has commits that haven't
    been pushed to GitHub yet. Example: if you commit 3 times locally but never
    push, it says "3 ahead." Right now: 0 ahead — everything on GitHub matches.

* THE SCHEDULED AUTO-COMMIT (Vistamations-GitCommit):
  - Runs every 2 days at 18:00 AEST. Last ran: 2026-08-10 18:00.
  - Next run: 2026-08-12 18:00.
  - When it runs, it auto-commits any changed files AND pushes to GitHub.
  - IT DOES NOT RUN ON MANUAL COMMITS — only the scheduled task triggers it.
  - If you NEVER want auto-commits, disable the task in Windows Task Scheduler.
  - Currently: NO files have been committed since 2026-08-10 23:04.

SECTION 2: WHAT IS "MAIN"? WHAT IS "EVIDENCE-REGISTRY"? HOW DO THEY RELATE?
----------------------------------------------------------------------------

  - Repository URL: https://github.com/petehops89-jpg/command_control
  - This repo contains ALL branches. Branches are lines of commits within

    (except git worktrees, which are temporary working copies).

  BRANCH: "main" (1 commit)
  ├── Created: 2026-08-07 04:22 AEST

  ├── Status: DEAD. Nothing has been built on main since day 1.

  BRANCH: "evidence-registry" (18 commits after main)
  ├── Created: 2026-08-09 02:08 AEST (auto-commit)

  │   Command Portal, Olivia Gate, Media Centre, Mya, Cloudflare D1,
  │   Workers, security modules, 4-value ID restructure, all Pete files.
  ├── Status: ACTIVE. This is where you are. This is where all work lives.
  │   git checkout evidence-registry = switch here. You are here now.
  └── GitHub: pushed to origin/evidence-registry

  BRANCH: "publishing-engine-v2" (1 commit after main)
  ├── Contains: Monitor1 dashboard, 5-dominion classification, value scoring

* YOU ARE ON: evidence-registry. That is correct. Do not switch to main.

SECTION 3: GITHUB REPOSITORIES, BRANCHES, AND THE SYSTEM RELATIONSHIP
---------------------------------------------------------------------

* THE SYSTEM RELATIONSHIP (plain English):

    GitHub (https://github.com/petehops89-jpg/command_control)
    └── Repository: "command_control" (ONE repo, not multiple)
        ├── Branch: "main"          ← pushed to GitHub (origin/main)
        ├── Branch: "evidence-registry"  ← pushed to GitHub (origin/evidence-registry)
        └── Branch: "publishing-engine-v2"  ← pushed to GitHub

    Your computer (C:\vistamations-music)
    └── Local clone of the "command_control" repo
        ├── Currently on branch: evidence-registry
        └── Files reflect that branch

    Cloud Sub-System (Cloudflare Workers + GCP Vertex AI)
    └── Separate from GitHub — deployed separately via wrangler / gcloud CLI

* GITHUB vs YOUR COMPUTER:
  - GitHub is the REMOTE copy. It's on the internet.
  - Your computer is the LOCAL copy. C:\vistamations-music.
  - `git push` = send your local commits to GitHub.
  - `git pull` = download new commits from GitHub to your computer.
  - Auto-commit pushes to GitHub. Manual work stays local until pushed.

* WHAT "ORIGIN" MEANS:
  - "origin" = the GitHub remote URL (https://github.com/petehops89-jpg/command_control)
  - "origin/main" = the main branch AS IT EXISTS ON GITHUB
  - "origin/evidence-registry" = the evidence-registry branch AS IT EXISTS ON GITHUB
  - These are read-only mirrors. They update when you push or pull.

---

SECTION 4: WHAT ARE PULL REQUESTS? ARE THEY APPLICABLE TO THE SYSTEM?
---------------------------------------------------------------------

* WHAT A PULL REQUEST (PR) IS:
  - A pull request is a formal request on GitHub saying: "Please merge branch A
    into branch B." It's the standard way teams collaborate on GitHub.
  - Example: "Merge the new Media Centre feature (my branch) into evidence-registry
    (the main development branch)."
  - PRs allow code review — another person looks at your changes before they merge.
  - PRs can trigger automated tests (CI/CD) before allowing a merge.

* ARE PULL REQUESTS APPLICABLE TO THIS SYSTEM?
  - YES, but NOT YET. PRs are useful when:
    a) Multiple people work on the same repo (not applicable — only Pete works here)
    b) Automated tests exist to validate changes before merging (not applicable —
       zero tests, zero CI/CD)
    c) You want to review changes before merging them into a stable branch (the
       intended workflow once the system matures)

  - What WOULD make sense for Vistamations:
    * evidence-registry → merge into main (when main is reactivated as a stable
      "production" branch)
    * Feature branches → pull requests into evidence-registry (when distinct
      features are developed in isolation by different agents)
    * Pull requests with required checks (once tests + CI exist)

  - CURRENTLY: PRs are NOT being used. You are working directly on evidence-registry
    without branching for individual features. This is fine for a solo developer at
    the current stage. PRs become necessary when the system has:
    - Multiple contributors
    - Stable vs development branch separation
    - Automated test gates (CI/CD pipeline)

SECTION 5: AGENT INSTRUCTIONS, MEMORY, AND AGENTS.MD
-----------------------------------------------------

* WHAT AGENTS.MD IS:
  - AGENTS.md (created this session, 11/08/2026) is the system-level agent briefing
    file at C:\vistamations-music\AGENTS.md.
  - It is read by Kilo (the AI tool) at the START of every session. Every agent
    (regardless of mode/role) sees this file first.
  - It replaces the old `.vscode/instructions.txt` which was a single-line note.
    AGENTS.md is the comprehensive version.

* WHAT AGENTS.MD CONTAINS:
  - System identity (what Vistamations is and what it builds)
  - Terminology bridge (Vistamations terms ↔ industry terms)
  - Full system architecture diagram (Local Sub-System + Cloud Sub-System)
  - Agent roster (10 agents, roles, runtime, reporting chain)
  - Command list (xinitiate, xstatus, xtelemetry, xsync, xclear, xpair, xchat-save)
  - Git branch clarification (evidence-registry is the active branch)
  - System health status (46%)

* WHERE AGENTS.MD FITS IN THE AGENT INSTRUCTION HIERARCHY:

  LAYER 1: AGENTS.md (system root)
    → Read by ALL agents. Defines what the system IS.
    
  LAYER 2: .kilo/modes/*.md (per-agent mode files)
    → Read by individual agents. Defines what each agent DOES.
    → Gordon: .kilo/modes/gordon.md (Docker orchestration)
    → Big Brother: .kilo/modes/big-brother.md (architecture + code review)
    → etc.

  LAYER 3: personas/*.json (per-agent identity data)
    → Structured data: reporting chain, capabilities, active projects.
    → Currently: only 2 of 10 exist (Big Brother AG006, Terence AG009)

  LAYER 4: .vscode/instructions.txt (legacy 1-line note)
    → The old instruction file. Now superseded by AGENTS.md.
    → Can be deleted or kept as historical reference.

  LAYER 5: Project memory (.kilo/memory/ + Kilo knowledge graph)
    → Persistent memory across sessions (decisions, facts, corrections).
    → Read by agents during task execution.
    → Also: .memory-bank/*.md (productContext, decisionLog, etc.)

* THE AGENTS.MD QUESTION:
  - Pete asked: "I created a separate file. Is it OK to transfer and consolidate
    to .md? Is that what agents prefer?"
  - ANSWER: YES. AGENTS.md is the standard convention. Kilo (the AI tool) 
    automatically reads AGENTS.md at session startup. Agents do not need to be
    told to read it — it's injected into their context automatically.
  - The old .vscode/instructions.txt was a single-line note. AGENTS.md replaces
    it with a comprehensive document.
  - All system directives have been MERGED into AGENTS.md. Nothing was lost.
  - .vscode/instructions.txt still exists and can be deleted — AGENTS.md is the
    canonical source.

* AGENT MEMORY SYSTEMS (OVERVIEW):
  - Kilo project memory (.kilo/memory/) — durable facts, decisions, corrections
  - Knowledge graph — entity-relation graph (currently EMPTY)
  - Redis — key-value cache (currently EMPTY)
  - Memory bank (.memory-bank/) — 5 markdown docs (stale)
  - File stores — JSON on disk (Olivia queue, projects, assets)
  - AGENTS.md — session-injected briefing (does not persist between sessions —

  | API Endpoints     | 100%  | 17 routes verified                     |
  | Scheduled Tasks   | 100%  | 6 tasks operational                    |

  | Memory Systems    | 10%   | Knowledge graph empty, Redis empty     |
  | Test Coverage     | 0%    | Zero tests exist                       |
  | CI/CD             | 0%    | No pipeline                            |
  | Agent Auto-Dispatch | 30% | Simple patterns only, no daemon        |
  | Documentation     | 60%   | Memory bank exists but stale           |
  | Security          | 40%   | Hardcoded secrets, no audit            |
  | AVERAGE           | 46%   | Health is infrastructure OK, logic WIP |

* Command Control Status Dots (the green dots on index.html):
  - These ARE live — they poll API endpoints every 10 seconds.
  - /api/health, /api/olivia/queue, /api/research/links, /api/publications, /api/metrics
  - A green dot means the endpoint returned a valid response. It does NOT mean
    the system is "46% healthy" — it means that specific service is responding.
  - The 46% figure is a human audit. The Status Dots are machine-level health probes.
    They answer different questions.
